paragraph: Mahwah is running hot in both tiers right now. Single-family homes posted 63 sales over six months at a median of $1,050,000, with a 1.03 sale-to-list ratio, 60 percent of homes selling above asking, and a median of 18 days on market. That is a real seller's market, and multiple offer situations are common. Condos and townhouses are the higher-volume tier at 102 sales and a median of $513,750, moving even faster at 14 days on market with three quarters of sales closing above list. Mahwah's single-family range is unusually wide, from a handful of land and teardown-level sales under $150,000 up to $2,600,000, so the median tells you less here than in a town with more uniform housing stock. On the seasonal read, single-family volume climbed steadily into June and July while the July median fell to $934,750 from June's $1,312,500. Volume up and median down means the mix shifted toward smaller homes, not that values dropped. Condo medians have drifted from $553,500 in May to $510,000 in July, which tracks the normal arc. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. Both tiers are competitive. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle of a townhouse.
